title: U.S. House · California's 1st District
area: A rural district covering far northern California, including Doug LaMalfa's former Sutter County base and surrounding North State counties, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

Previous incumbent Doug LaMalfa did not run for the seat in the 2026 regular election. James Gallagher won a 2026 special election for the seat and assumed office on June 11, 2026, ahead of the regular general election for the next full term.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, James Gallagher (R) placed first with 42.1% (92,975 votes) and Mike McGuire (D) placed second with 41.8% (92,121 votes) out of 220,595 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: James Gallagher
candidates.ballotNote: Won a 2026 special election for this seat and placed first in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary for the full term
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since June 11, 2026); previously California State Assembly Minority Leader (2022-2025)

summary.text: James Gallagher is an attorney and farmer from Sutter County who served on the Sutter County Board of Supervisors and then in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2026, including as Assembly Minority Leader from 2022 to 2025. He won the June 2, 2026 special election outright to fill the House seat left vacant by the death of Rep. Doug LaMalfa and is also running for a full term. His stated campaign messages are lower taxes, lower fees and fewer regulations, tougher laws against crime, and protecting farms and businesses from regulation.

background.text: Born in Yuba City in 1981 and attended local schools, according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response; he describes himself as a descendant of Irish immigrants who settled in northern California in the early 1800s.
Earned a high school diploma from East Nicolaus High School, a B.A. from UC Berkeley, and a law degree (J.D.) from UC Davis; he also completed an Assembly Fellowship in Sacramento.
Worked as an attorney in a practice centered on business and agriculture and is a partner in his family's rice farm.
Served on the Sutter County Board of Supervisors for six years before joining the Assembly.

Represented California's Third Assembly District from 2014 to 2026; Roll Call describes the district as an inland district centered on Chico. His Assembly committee service included the Judiciary Committee, on which he was Vice Chair.
Was Assembly Minority Leader from 2022 to 2025, leading Republican legislators in opposing the 2025 redistricting effort; Roll Call reports he stepped down as caucus leader in September 2025.

Roll Call reports that the Public Policy Institute of California credited him with paying particular attention to small businesses and farms and with dozens of enacted bills, including a measure to facilitate housing relief for victims of the 2018 Camp Fire.

Won the June 2, 2026 special primary for California's 1st District with more than 60 percent of the vote, avoiding an August runoff, and was sworn in on June 10, 2026 to complete the term of the late Rep. Doug LaMalfa; he also advanced from the regular June 2 primary for the full term.

According to his Ballotpedia survey response, he is married and lives in Sutter County with his family, and is passionate about wildfire mitigation, water storage, supporting farms and small businesses, and neighborhood safety.

priorities.text: Lists three key campaign messages: making life more affordable for North State families through lower taxes, fees and regulations; enacting tougher laws to protect communities from crime; and protecting farms and businesses from excessive government regulation.
Says he is personally passionate about wildfire mitigation, water storage, and supporting farms and small businesses.
priorities.quote: Wildfire mitigation. Water storage. Supporting farms and small businesses. Keeping our neighborhoods safe.

record.text: Served as California Assembly Minority Leader from 2022 to 2025.
Served on the Sutter County Board of Supervisors for six years before joining the Assembly.
Won a 2026 special election for California's 1st Congressional District and assumed office June 11, 2026.

candidates.name: Mike McGuire
candidates.ballotNote: Placed second in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: California State Senator, District 2 (since 2014); former Senate President pro Tempore (2024-2025)

summary.text: Mike McGuire is a Democratic California State Senator who first won public office at age 19 on the Healdsburg School Board, later serving on the Healdsburg City Council and Sonoma County Board of Supervisors before his 2014 election to the State Senate. He served as Senate Majority Leader and then as President pro Tempore from 2024 to 2025. He announced his run for Congress in November 2025 and advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from Sonoma State University in 2002.
Worked in the radio and television industries.
First elected to public office in 1998 at age 19 to the Healdsburg School Board, then elected to the Healdsburg City Council in 2004.
Elected to the Sonoma County Board of Supervisors in 2010.

Elected to the California State Senate in 2014, defeating Republican Lawrence R. Wiesner 70%-30%, and re-elected in 2018 and 2022 with more than 66% of the vote each time; he represents District 2, which covers Marin, Sonoma, Lake, Mendocino, Humboldt, Trinity and Del Norte counties.

Selected as Senate Majority Leader in January 2022 by then-President pro Tempore Toni Atkins, and elected Senate President pro Tempore on February 5, 2024; Ballotpedia reports he was the first senator from California's northern coast chosen to lead the Senate since 1866.

Agreed in June 2025 to step down as Senate leader so S. Monique Limon could succeed him, and left the position on November 17, 2025; he announced his congressional campaign the same month. The Associated Press, as quoted by Ballotpedia, reported he authored legislation on marine life, cannabis farmers, cellphone service during power outages, and wildfire impacts.

record.text: Serves as Chair of the Senate Rules Committee and Chair of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Committee in the 2025-2026 session.
Elected to the California State Senate representing District 2 in 2014.

researchNotes: Mike McGuire has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current campaign website content was found for this House race, so his stated priorities and issue positions could not be documented; his California State Senate record is summarized instead. James Gallagher's official House issues pages (gallagher.house.gov/issues) were checked, along with his press releases and Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; the issues pages describe general topic areas (agriculture, jobs, transportation, veterans, national security) without statements that directly address any of the 15 tracked issue statements, so no positions were added for him. Biography gaps: Gallagher's official House 'About' page contains no biography, so his background draws on Ballotpedia, his survey response and Roll Call; McGuire has no current campaign biography or survey, so his background draws on Ballotpedia and does not cover his pre-2010 employers in detail.
